kategorie:
**

Travel Stories from Tirol

** **

Discover the magic of Tirol through the eyes of travelers who have experienced its breathtaking landscapes, charming towns, and unforgettable adventures.

** --- **

Innsbruck – Where Tradition Meets Modernity

** **

Innsbruck, the sparkling capital of Tirol, blends alpine grandeur with vibrant city life. Visitors rave about strolling through the Old Town, admiring the **Goldenes Dachl**, and indulging in hearty **Tiroler Gröstl** or a slice of **Kaiserschmarrn** at a cozy café. The **Nordkette** cable car offers jaw-dropping views of the Alps, while the **Alpenzoo** delights animal lovers with its high-altitude exhibits.

** **
*"The energy of Innsbruck is infectious—whether you're hiking in the **Karwendel** mountains or sipping a **Schnaps** at a rustic **Hütte** after a long day on the slopes!"*
** --- **

Zillertal – A Valley of Endless Adventures

** **

The **Zillertal** is a paradise for outdoor enthusiasts. Skiers and snowboarders flock to **Ahorn** and **Gerlos** for world-class slopes, while hikers explore the **Zillertaler Höhenweg**, a scenic trail with panoramic vistas. In summer, the valley transforms into a playground for rafting, mountain biking, and visiting the **Zillertal Arena**, where thrill-seekers can try bungee jumping or paragliding.

** **
*"The **Zillertal** is pure escapism—crystal-clear lakes, lush meadows, and **Hütten** serving the best **Käsespätzle** you’ve ever tasted!"*
** --- **

Ötztal – The Land of Glaciers and Legends

** **

Deep in the heart of the Alps lies the **Ötztal**, home to the **Ötztal Glacier**, one of Europe’s most accessible glaciers. Adventurers trek to the **Hochalpenstraße**, a breathtaking road leading to the **Hochzeiger** peak, while culture seekers explore the **Ötztal Museum** or the historic **St. Sigmund im Sellrain**. Don’t miss the chance to try **Ötztaler Speck**—a local delicacy that’s as flavorful as it is famous.

** **
*"The **Ötztal** feels like stepping into another world—glaciers, waterfalls, and **Hütten** where the **Apfelstrudel** is served with a side of pure serenity."*
** --- **

Lech am Arlberg – The Ultimate Ski & Relaxation Hub

** **

**Lech am Arlberg** is a ski legend, but its charm extends far beyond winter sports. In summer, the **Arlberg Trail** invites hikers to explore alpine meadows, while the **Lechfall** waterfall offers a stunning natural spectacle. The town’s après-ski scene is legendary, with **Stüberl** (traditional taverns) serving up **Tiroler Wein** and **Kaiserschmarrn** until the early hours.

** **
*"**Lech am Arlberg** is where the mountains meet the party—whether you're shredding the **Pitztal Glacier** or unwinding with a **Schnaps** and a view of the **Vergletscherte Täler**."*
** --- **

Explore More of Tirol

** **

From the fairy-tale charm of **Swoveland** to the rugged beauty of **Kaunergrat**, Tirol’s travel stories are as diverse as its landscapes. Whether you're seeking adventure, relaxation, or a taste of **Tiroler Gastfreundschaft**, every corner of this region promises an unforgettable journey.

teaser: The **Ötztal** is the most active valley in **Tirol**: glacier hikes, via ferratas, mountain bike trails, white-water rafting, and Austria’s highest church – the ultimate guide for adventure and relaxation.
inhalt:
The **Ötztal** is far more than just a valley—it’s one of the most diverse outdoor regions in the Alps. Stretching across **530 square kilometers**, it rises from **Oetz** at **812 meters** all the way up to the glaciers of the inner **Ötztal**. Nowhere else in **Tirol** will you find such a high concentration of activities: over **1,000 kilometers** of marked hiking trails, three glacier ski resorts, **Tirol’s** tallest waterfall, the longest suspension bridge in the state, and one of Europe’s most modern thermal spas. The entire valley is crisscrossed by a dense network of well-developed hiking and mountain biking trails, captivating nature lovers and adrenaline junkies alike. Add to that around **17,000 residents** living in the charming towns of **Oetz**, **[Sautens](/orte/sautens/), Umhausen, [Längenfeld](/orte/laengenfeld/), and [Sölden](/orte/soelden/)**—each with its own character and unique offerings for guests. This guide takes you on a journey of discovery through **Tirol’s** extreme valley—from the gentle hills at the valley entrance to the icy heights of the **Wildspitze**.

---

### **Oetz and Umhausen – Active Start at the Valley Entrance**

The gateway to the **Ötztal** is formed by the municipalities of **Oetz** and **Umhausen**. **Oetz**, at **812 meters**, is the perfect starting point for active travelers who want to explore the valley step by step. The town is home to one of the region’s largest outdoor centers, where you can book everything from climbing courses to canyoning and whitewater rafting on the **Ötztaler Ache**. The whitewater activities on the **Ache** are among the valley’s most popular offerings—the rapids (class III to IV) provide a serious adrenaline rush, and guided tours are also suitable for beginners.

The absolute highlight in **Oetz** is the **Stuibenfall**, **Tirol’s** tallest waterfall at **159 meters**. The **Stuibenfall-Wasserfallweg** trail leads right past the roaring mist—an easy, family-friendly hike, described in detail in the article [Wanderwege im Ötztal](/magazin/wanderwege-oetztal). Since **2024**, the **Stuibenfall-Hängebrücke** has also spanned the gorge at **80 meters** high—one of **Tirol’s** most spectacular bridges and a must-visit for all valley guests. The view down into the roaring gorge is not for the faint-hearted, but the perspective of the waterfall from the bridge is simply unmatched.

Just upstream lies **Umhausen**, at **1,031 meters**, the highest municipality in the front **Ötztal**. Here, you’ll find the **Ötzi-Dorf**, an authentic reconstruction of a Copper Age settlement from the time of **Ötzi**, the Iceman. The open-air museum is not only a cultural highlight but also a popular outing for families. Nearby, the **Naturbadeteich Umhausen** invites you to cool off in crystal-clear mountain water—ideal after a long hike.

#### **Activities in Oetz and Umhausen at a Glance:**
- **Stuibenfall-Wasserfallweg** (easy, 4.5 km, 2 hours)
- **Ötzi-Dorf** visit (approx. 1.5 hours)
- Whitewater rafting on the **Ötztaler Ache** (season: May–September)
- Canyoning at the **Stuibenfall** (guided tours, from €90 per person)
- Mountain biking in the **Tumpener Tal** (moderate, 25 km)
- **Naturbadeteich Umhausen** (free entry)
- **Area 47 High Ropes Course** in the neighboring **Inntal** (20 minutes by car)

---

### **Längenfeld – Between Aqua Dome and Piburger See**

**Längenfeld**, with its **4,600 inhabitants**, is the largest municipality in the inner **Ötztal** and a true all-rounder. The town at **1,179 meters** uniquely combines wellness, hiking, and winter activities. It stretches for several kilometers along the **Ötztaler Ache**, offering an impressive density of accommodations, gastronomy, and leisure activities.

The landmark of **Längenfeld** is the **Aqua Dome**—one of **Tirol’s** most famous thermal spas. Three striking glass domes house indoor and outdoor pools with thermal water heated to **34–40°C**, sourced from **1,800 meters** below the surface. The alpine spa features a generous sauna panorama with views of the surrounding **3,000-meter peaks**, making it the perfect retreat on rainy days. **Tip:** If you want to combine an active holiday with wellness, book the **"Wandern & Baden" combo card**, available in many hotels. The **Aqua Dome** is open daily from **9:00 AM to 10:00 PM**; a day pass costs from **€28** for adults, with discounted rates for families and children.

Hiking enthusiasts will find plenty to love in **Längenfeld**. The **Ötztal Nature Park** begins just above the town, offering a variety of routes through untouched nature. Particularly recommended is the circular hike to the **Piburger See**, a **smaragd-green mountain lake** at **1,280 meters**, one of **Tirol’s** warmest bathing lakes. The gentle loop is also suitable for inexperienced hikers and families—detailed descriptions of this and other tours can be found in the article [Wanderwege im Ötztal](/magazin/wanderwege-oetztal). In summer, the lake reaches water temperatures of up to **24°C**, making it one of the few truly swimmable mountain lakes in the region.

Another highlight in **Längenfeld** is the **Burgruine Längenfeld**, a **13th-century castle ruin** perched above the town. From here, you’ll enjoy a fantastic view over the entire valley. The climb to the ruin takes about **20 minutes** and is also manageable for children.

#### **Längenfeld’s Top Offers:**
- **Aqua Dome** – Day pass from **€28**, open daily **9:00 AM–10:00 PM**
- **Piburger See** – Circular trail, **2.5 km**, ~45 minutes
- **Ötztal Nature Park** – Guided tours (June–October)
- **Längenfeld Cross-Country Ski Trail** – **15 km** groomed track (winter)
- **Via Ferrata at Burgruine Längenfeld** – moderate, **1.5 hours**

---

### **Sölden – Glacier Spectacle and 3,000-Meter Panorama**

**Sölden**, at **1,368 meters** and with around **3,000 inhabitants**, is the heart of the **Ötztal**, best known for its two glacier ski resorts. But even in summer, **Sölden** offers an enormous range of activities for active holidaymakers. The two glaciers—the **Rettenbachferner** and the **Tiefenbachferner**—make **Sölden** one of Austria’s most snow-reliable ski areas and offer spectacular hiking and adventure opportunities even in high summer.

The absolute highlight is the **Söldener Gletscherwelt**. The **Gletscherexpress** cable car takes you up to the **Tiefenbachferner** at over **3,000 meters**. Once at the top, you’ll find breathtaking glacier hikes (guided only!), a stunning view of the **Ötztal Alps**, and the **007 ELEMENTS**, an interactive **James Bond** exhibition at the summit of the **Gaislachkohl (3,048 m)**. This spectacular structure, which served as a filming location for the **Bond** movie *"Spectre"*, is one of the Alps’ most unusual attractions—entry **€24**, open daily from **10:00 AM to 6:00 PM**. The observation deck on the roof offers an unmatched **360-degree view** of around **140 peaks** in the **Ötztal** and **Stubaier Alps**.

For hikers, the **Söldener Bergwelt** with over **60 kilometers** of marked trails is a paradise. Particularly beautiful is the hike from the **Gaislachkohl (3,048 m)** via the **Similaun** back to the mid-station—a high-alpine panoramic hike that’s also doable without glacier experience. The **Sölden** mountain railways operate seven lift systems in summer as well, taking you to the heights. A day pass costs around **€35**. Those who prefer to hike up on foot will find marked ascent routes through the impressive mountain scenery.

#### **Sölden in Numbers:**
- Highest point: **Wildspitze (3,774 m)** (highest peak in **Tirol**)
- Summer mountain railways: **7 lift systems** in operation
- Glacier option: Open year-round (skiing possible even in summer)
- **James Bond**: **007 ELEMENTS** – a unique experience at **3,048 m**
- Gastronomy: **70+ huts, inns, and restaurants** throughout the town

---

### **The Innermost Ötztal – Obergurgl and Hochgurgl**

Further up the valley, at **1,930 meters**, lies **Obergurgl**—Austria’s highest parish. The village is a paradise for those who prefer it quieter and more authentic, yet still want plenty of activities. **Obergurgl** is surrounded by **20 peaks over 3,000 meters**, offering an alpine landscape unmatched in its grandeur.

**Obergurgl** and the neighboring **Hochgurgl (2,150 m)** form the so-called **Gurglertal**—a side valley of the **Ötztal** that enchants visitors with its alpine authenticity, especially in summer. Here, numerous high-alpine hikes begin, including the ascent to the **Gurgler Alm (2,162 m)**, a gentle hike with a grand glacier panorama, as well as the more challenging climb of the **Hohen Mut (2,600 m)**, rewarded with a **360-degree panorama** over the **Ötztal Alps**. From the **Hohen Mut**, you have a direct view of the glacier and the impressive rock landscape of the **Gurgler Kamm**.

The **Ötztal Premium-Wanderweg 001 – Hohe Mut** is one of the region’s most beautiful high-altitude trails. The start is in **Obergurgl**; the gondola takes you to **2,600 meters**, and then you hike along the ridge with fantastic views back into the valley. The hike takes about **3–4 hours** and is of moderate difficulty, requiring sure footing. A stop at the **Schönwieshütte (2,266 m)** is highly recommended—the homemade **Kaiserschmarrn** with a glacier view is legendary and a culinary highlight of every tour.

#### **Outdoor in Obergurgl-Hochgurgl:**
- Top hike: **Hohen Mut** – summit panorama (moderate, 4h)
- Family hike: **Gurgler Alm** (easy, 2h)
- Hidden gem: **Schönwieshütte** – **Kaiserschmarrn** with glacier view
- Climbing: **Obergurgl** climbing park with routes up to **UIAA VI**
- Mountain biking: **Gurgler Mountainbike-Trail** – **35 km**, challenging

---

### **The Ötztal Premium-Wanderwelt – Award-Winning Trails for Every Taste**

The **Ötztal** has developed a special system to help travelers navigate: the **Ötztal Premium-Wanderwelt**. Around **20 carefully selected routes** have been certified for quality, scenic beauty, and experiential value. Each **Premium-Wanderweg** (identified by numbers **001 to 020**) offers a unique nature experience—from easy family hikes to multi-day hut tours.

What makes the **Premium-Ways** special: They are maintained year-round, the signage is up-to-date, and at the starting points, there are clear information boards. Many trails are accessible via regular bus connections (**Ötztal-Shuttle**, free with the **Ötztal Premium Card**) even without a car. The trails are categorized by difficulty (easy, moderate, difficult), with most falling into the moderate range and requiring basic hiking experience.

A selection of the best **Premium-Wanderwege**:

**PWW 004 – Rotmoosferner (Glacier Educational Trail)** – A unique insight into the world of glaciers. Over **6 km (3h)**, the trail runs alongside the **Rotmoosferner** and explains the formation and retreat of glaciers at **15 stations**. The tour starts in **Obergurgl** and is of moderate difficulty. Sturdy footwear and weatherproof clothing are essential, as even in high summer, icy temperatures can occur on the glacier.

**PWW 008 – Geierpfad** – The most adventurous trail in the entire **Ötztal**. Over **8 km** and **500 meters** of elevation gain, the via ferrata-like path runs along the cliff face high above the valley. Secured passages, ladders, and bridges make this a thrilling experience for experienced hikers. Duration: ~4 hours. **Only for those fearless of heights** and with appropriate equipment (via ferrata set recommended)!

**PWW 012 – Piburger See Runde** – The already mentioned easy loop around the **emerald-green mountain lake**. Ideal for families, inexperienced hikers, and as an afternoon stroll. Duration: **45 minutes**, minimal elevation gain. Perfect as an introduction to an active holiday or as a finale after a day at the **Aqua Dome**.
